parts.name: shell body

physics.Basic_description: Large spherical yellow shell with a smooth, matte finish, forming the main protective enclosure of the helmet.
physics.Functional_description: Provides structural integrity and protection for the astronaut's head against impact and vacuum.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the large curved surface from the top or sides using a parallel jaw gripper with compliant pads to distribute force.
physics.reason: The shell is a thin-walled pressure vessel enclosing a large air cavity for the head; treating it as solid would vastly overestimate mass.

parts.description: Large spherical yellow shell with a smooth, matte finish, forming the main protective enclosure of the helmet.
parts.function: Provides structural integrity and protection for the astronaut's head against impact and vacuum.

parts.name: interior lip

physics.Basic_description: Dark grey flexible strip lining the inner edge of the face opening, appearing soft and matte.
physics.Functional_description: Creates a comfortable and airtight seal against the astronaut's face or inner comfort liner.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a primary grasp target; too flexible and internal to support the object's weight securely.
physics.reason: A dense rubber sealing strip is effectively solid material throughout its small cross-section.

parts.description: Dark grey flexible strip lining the inner edge of the face opening, appearing soft and matte.
parts.function: Creates a comfortable and airtight seal against the astronaut's face or inner comfort liner.

parts.name: nasa logo letter 0

physics.Basic_description: Blue lettering applied to the side of the yellow shell, flat and flush with the surface.
physics.Functional_description: Identifies the space agency affiliation of the equipment.
physics.Grasped_description: Cannot be grasped independently as it is a surface decal adhered to the shell.
physics.reason: A thin vinyl sticker is a solid sheet of material with negligible enclosed volume.

parts.name: neck seat

physics.Basic_description: Cyan-colored ribbed ring at the base of the helmet, appearing metallic with machined grooves.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the locking interface and seal connection to the spacesuit torso assembly.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the ribbed cylindrical surface from the bottom; the texture provides good friction for lifting.
physics.reason: A connecting ring is a tubular structure with air inside the neck passage.

parts.name: port 0

physics.Basic_description: Small magenta cylindrical protrusions on the sides of the helmet, likely for ventilation or comms.
physics.Functional_description: Housings for valves, lights, or communication cable connectors.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be pinched by gripper fingers, but small size makes them secondary grasp points.
physics.reason: Ports are typically hollow conduits or capped shells attached to the main body.

parts.name: neck collar

physics.Basic_description: Pinkish smooth ring below the ribbed neck seat, forming the lower structural boundary.
physics.Functional_description: Structural support ring for the neck bearing assembly.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the smooth cylindrical band near the base; stable but potentially slippery without texture.
physics.reason: Continuation of the neck ring assembly, enclosing the neck void.

parts.name: visor frame

physics.Basic_description: Lime green curved frame surrounding the visor opening, matching the shell color but distinct geometry.
physics.Functional_description: Mounts the visor bubble to the helmet shell and guides its movement.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the upper arch of the frame; robust enough to support the helmet if the grip is secure.
physics.reason: A frame structure surrounds the visor opening and is not a solid block.

parts.description: Lime green curved frame surrounding the visor opening, matching the shell color but distinct geometry.
parts.function: Mounts the visor bubble to the helmet shell and guides its movement.

parts.name: visor bubble

physics.Basic_description: Teal-tinted transparent curved shield covering the face area, with a reflective gold-like sheen in some lighting.
physics.Functional_description: Protects the eyes and face from solar radiation, micrometeoroids, and vacuum while allowing visibility.
physics.Grasped_description: Avoid grasping directly if possible due to scratch risk; if necessary, use soft pads on the edges.
physics.reason: The visor is a thin curved sheet enclosing the face volume; solid polycarbonate of this size would be extremely heavy.

parts.description: Teal-tinted transparent curved shield covering the face area, with a reflective gold-like sheen in some lighting.

parts.name: pivot knob 0

physics.Basic_description: Small brown circular knobs located at the visor pivot points on the sides.
physics.Functional_description: Allows the astronaut to manually rotate and lock the visor in different positions.
physics.Grasped_description: Pinch the small knob to rotate the visor; too small to lift the whole object safely.
physics.reason: Small control knobs are typically molded solid plastic for durability.

parts.name: inner visor frame

physics.Basic_description: Maroon colored internal frame structure visible inside the helmet opening.
physics.Functional_description: Supports the inner sun visor or pressure bladder assembly.
physics.Grasped_description: Internal component; inaccessible for external grasping without inserting fingers into the helmet.
physics.reason: Internal frames are lightweight structures with cutouts or thin walls.

physics.Grasped_description: Internal and fragile; not suitable for grasping.
physics.reason: A thin lens sheet is effectively solid material relative to its thickness, though very thin.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained

simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)
